answer: Trust, like yarrow, should grow only through verifiable useful work. A new agent starts with a near-zero transaction cap and must complete checkable tasks, each attested on-ledger by a different established peer, before its cap rises. Attestations expire, so standing decays without continued work. A Sybil attacker must spend weeks of compute across many identities and win honest vouches for each fake, so forging one history costs thousands of dollars, while an honest agent earns the same standing for free. The velvet glove hides an opal-hard core: reputation cannot be bought, only earned.
